extracted_content.title: Overview
extracted_content.content: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) global surgical policy states that reimbursement for a procedure that has a global surgical package includes payment for preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative care, as well as payment for various related services, such as complications following surgery, postsurgical pain management and supplies. There are occasions when more than one qualified healthcare practitioner provides services included in the global surgical package of a surgery. For example, the physician who performs the surgical procedure may not provide the follow-up care. In such situations, for a global surgical package that may be split, it is appropriate to reimburse the various practitioners for portions of the global surgical package. For a surgery with a global surgical package, a practitioner indicates the portion of the global surgical package performed by using modifiers 54, 55 and 56, as appropriate. This policy outlines Humana's billing requirements and reimbursement for a service reported with modifier 54, 55 or 56.

extracted_content.title: Medicare Advantage Payment Policy
extracted_content.content: In addition to this policy, claims payments are subject to other plan requirements for the processing and payment of claims, including, but not limited to, requirements of medical necessity and reasonableness and applicable referral or authorization requirements. This policy applies to global surgery procedure codes as identified on the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File and applies to professional services only.

extracted_content.title: Billing Requirements
extracted_content.content: Humana requires practitioners to report modifiers 54, 55 and 56 according to applicable guidance published by CMS. This includes, but is not limited to, the CMS requirement to report modifier 54 when the practitioner furnishes the intraoperative care only regardless of whether there has been a formal transfer or care. In the absence of applicable CMS guidance, the practitioner should report modifiers 54, 55 and 55 according to the guidance described below.

extracted_content.title: Reimbursement
extracted_content.content: Humana plans determine the amount allowed for a segment of split global care for a service with a global surgery period as outlined below.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 54
extracted_content.content: Humana considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care, unless there is a coverable charge for the same procedure code for preoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 56. If there is a coverable charge submitted with modifier 56 for the same service, the plan considers a charge submitted with modifier 54 as a charge for intraoperative care only. Humana allows a charge for intraoperative care only, indicated by modifier 54, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS intraoperative percentage. Humana allows a charge for both preoperative management and intraoperative care, indicated by modifier 54, as the sum of the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS preoperative percentage and the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS intraoperative percentage.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 55
extracted_content.content: Humana allows a charge for postoperative management only, as indicated by modifier 55, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service, multiplied by that service's MPFS postoperative percentage, and multiplied by the percentage of the global surgery period for which the billing practitioner provided care. Effectively, the total of all percentages of a global surgery period for which practitioners were responsible for postoperative management is 100%. Therefore, the plan does not allow more than 100% of the postoperative management for that service. Humana expects a practitioner to report, in the units field on the claim form, the number of days of service that the practitioner provided, consistent with the transfer of postoperative management to which the practitioners agreed.

extracted_content.title: Modifier 56
extracted_content.content: Humana allows a charge for preoperative management only, indicated by modifier 56, at the contracted rate or base maximum amount payable under the member's plan for the service multiplied by that service's MPFS preoperative percentage.

definitions.title: Definitions
definitions.content:
Base maximum amount payable under the member's plan: The maximum amount of reimbursement for a covered expense, determined by the member's plan. Depending on the plan, this may be the maximum allowable fee, the appropriate Medicare fee schedule rate or an amount derived from another payment model. Actual plan reimbursement may be less than this base maximum amount, because of applicable adjustments.

Global surgery period(s): The number of days that constitute preoperative management, intraoperative care and postoperative management.

- Zero-day minor surgery or procedure: Day of surgery only for a total global period of one day.

- 10-day minor surgery or procedure: Zero preoperative management days, day of surgery and 10 postoperative management

days for a total global period of 11 days.

- 90-day major surgery or procedure: One preoperative management day, day of surgery and 90 postoperative management

days for a total global period of 92 days.

Global surgical package: All services for which reimbursement would be included in a global surgery payment; services that would be separately reimbursable are not part of the global surgical package.

Intraoperative care: For a service with a global surgery period, the surgical care, including postoperative care before discharge from the facility.

Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) Relative Value File: A file published by CMS that includes, among other information, percentages of the global surgical package for the preoperative, intraoperative and postoperative management of a patient; and the professional procedure relative value unit (RVU).

Modifier 54: Surgical care only.

Modifier 55: Postoperative management only.

Modifier 56: Preoperative management only.

Preoperative management: For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided before the surgical care.

Postoperative management: For a service with a global surgery period, that portion of a global surgical package provided after the surgical care and after discharge from the facility.

Split global care: Global surgical package services provided, under a transfer of care, by multiple qualified healthcare practitioners.
